issue_context.title: API Proposal: Implement IEnumerable<> on various X509 collection types
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @bartonjs, @vcsjones, @krwq, @GrabYourPitchForks See info in area-owners.md if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
## Background and Motivation X509Certificate2Collection and related types implement the non-generic enumerable but not generic enumerable. This makes them harder to use with LINQ, and it's very common to see `.OfType()` used with these types, even though all of the elements of the collection are guaranteed to implement that type. This makes consumption both more cumbersome, more confusing, and more expensive. We can't change the signatures of the public GetEnumerator methods on these types, but we can at least implement the interfaces so that the OfType isn't necessary. ## Proposed API ```diff public class X509Certificate2Collection : X509CertificateCollection, + IEnumerable { ... } public sealed class X509Certificate2Enumerator : IEnumerator, + IEnumerator { ... } public sealed class X509ChainElementCollection : ICollection, + IEnumerable { ... } public sealed class X509ChainElementEnumerator : IEnumerator, + IEnumerator { ... } public sealed class X509ExtensionCollection : ICollection, + IEnumerable { ... } public sealed class X509ExtensionEnumerator : IEnumerator, + IEnumerator { ... } ``` All new interface method implementations would be explicit. (We could also consider implementing `ICollection` where the existing type implements `ICollection`.) Example commit: https://github.com/stephentoub/runtime/commit/d310e84f5b1918f5886edf640fdfee13cb01393d
Author: stephentoub
Assignees: -
Labels: `api-suggestion`, `area-System.Security`
Milestone: 6.0.0

If that's true, that's a bug, since the implementation assumes that's not true, e.g.
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ded66fc97eaeb9cefd4646cce431131cf8e8877c/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates/src/System/Security/Cryptography/X509Certificates/X509Certificate2Collection.cs#L38
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/82ca681cbac89d813a3ce397e0c665e6c051ed67/src/libraries/System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates/src/System/Security/Cryptography/X509Certificates/X509Certificate2Enumerator.cs#L22

I believe they can be added and removed, because of the members on X509CertificateCollection (the base class of X509Certificate2Collection), but it puts the collection in a bad state for indexing and enumerating.

I agree with the current proposal not making `X509CertificateCollection : IEnumerable<X509Certificate>` (since that would make the 2-coll be both-kinds enumerable), and I think we can safely ignore this corner case (being in no worse a state than we currently are).

In reality, no one instantiates X509Certificate(1), and no one derives from it (other than X509Certificate2), so it's not a major practical concern.
We could also override OnValidate to throw an exception if a non-X509Certificate2 is added, but it sounds like even that's not warranted.

Throwing that at SharpLab and looking at the IL, it looks like the argument to `collection.Cast<X509Certificate>` is ending up at CollectionBase.GetEnumerator, which returns an enumerator over the underlying ArrayList.

So in order to maintain compatibility in this case (if we care) we would need to explicitly re-implement IEnumerable.GetEnumerator to replicate the one coming from CollectionBase, instead of deferring to the stronger-typed X509Certificate2Collection.GetEnumerator.

review_comments: @bartonjs, opinion on this being explicitly implemented vs implicitly? (here and for the other dispose methods)
For a sealed type that most people never use directly where it's a no-op merely required by interface inheritance?  Nah.
